land.text: Cliopatria's Brycheiniog shape, the Usk and upper Wye country of south Powys: the page says it 'later formed the southern and larger part of the historic county of Brecknockshire'

predecessors.note: The infobox says 'Preceded by Roman Britain'; Cliopatria's equivalent is the Brythons row. The page dates the founding 'c.450' (infobox), 'mid-5th century' and 'probably ... by Irish raiders in the late fifth century' (text).

land.text: 'The lands of Brycheiniog became Bernard's Lordship of Brecknock' after 1093; the infobox names 'Lordship of Brecon'

successors.note: A Marcher lordship Cliopatria lacks (group eu-11-x). The infobox also names the Kingdom of Deheubarth: Rhys ap Tewdwr, 'king of Deheubarth', was killed at Brecon in April 1093, but no page opened says Deheubarth took Brycheiniog land.

capitals.name: Garth Madrun (Talgarth)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Talgarth'; the body spells it 'Garth Madrun'. The royal llys stormed by Æthelflæd on 19 June 916 stood 'in Llangorse lake' (a second seat, same text). Talgarth is not in the gazetteer's places table; the coordinates are the town's.

correction.text: unchanged: Cliopatria's first Brycheiniog shape (10 cells, 1,962 km2) used for 450-539

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 450-539: Cliopatria's first Brycheiniog shape begins in 540. The infobox says 'Founded by Brychan Brycheiniog: c.450'; the text 'Traditionally, it was founded by and named after a legendary Hiberno-Welsh prince named Brychan' and 'probably founded by Irish raiders in the late fifth century'. The page gives no area, so no comparison with the 1,962 km2 of the shape is possible; Cliopatria's first shape stands in for 450-539.

540-946, 1,962 km2 (10 cells: Powys 5, Herefordshire 2, and one each of Blaenau Gwent, Carmarthenshire and Merthyr Tydfil). The page: the kingdom 'later formed the southern and larger part of the historic county of Brecknockshire'; the page describes no boundaries and gives no area. Events inside the span move no border: the battle of Ffinnant in 848 (Brycheiniog men kill Ithel ap Hywel of Gwent), Elisse a vassal of Alfred 'in the 880s', the Norse devastation of 896, Æthelflæd's invasion of 916 and Tewdwr ap Elisse 'certainly ruling between 927 and 929'.

947-959, 2,006 km2: the same ten cells as the 540 shape (a vertex-level difference only). The Hywel Dda infobox lists Hywel as 'King of Brycheiniog c. 930 - 950' and the text says 'Brycheiniog seems also to have been left to Hywel's sons as well, but its history is unclear until' Elystan Glodrydd; Hywel is said to have ruled 'nearly all of Wales except for Morgannwg and Gwent'. A Deheubarth overlordship for the Seisyllwg ledger; the shape stands.

960-1055, 1,962 km2, the 540 shape again. The infobox ends the kingdom with the 'Death of Gryfydd ap Elisedd: c. 1045' while the text has the Normans destroy it after 1088-1095; Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1055 and no Brycheiniog row exists for 1056-1065 because its land lies inside Cliopatria's Gwynedd shape of those years (23,247 km2, 82 cells). The Gruffydd ap Llywelyn page: 1055 to 1063 he ruled all Wales ('the whole of Wales recognised him from about 1057').

correction.text: Brycheiniog proper, the 960 shape, restored when Gruffydd's realm was divided

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1063-1065: Brycheiniog proper again. Gruffydd ap Llywelyn died on 5 August 1063 and his realm 'was divided again into the traditional kingdoms'; Cliopatria keeps Brycheiniog's land inside its Gwynedd shape to 1065 and starts a Brycheiniog row in 1066. The page does not mention Brycheiniog (page silent): the restoration is read from 'the traditional kingdoms'.

correction.text: Brycheiniog proper without the Gwent and Morgannwg cells

keyframe_review.note: 1066-1071, 4,958 km2 as drawn (19 cells): Brycheiniog's ten cells plus nine cells that are Cliopatria's Gwent (5) and Morgannwg (4) shapes of 1055. The Gruffydd page has him seize Gwent and Morgannwg after 1055 ('around this time') and the realm divided again in 1063; no page opened has Brycheiniog ruling Gwent or Morgannwg. Those cells go back to the Gwent and Morgannwg dossiers (whose Cliopatria rows end in 1055).

correction.text: Brycheiniog proper less its eastern edge, without the Gwent and Morgannwg cells

keyframe_review.note: 1072-1084, 3,494 km2 as drawn (13 cells): Brycheiniog proper less two cells on its eastern and south-eastern edge (one in Herefordshire, one on the Gwent border near Crickhowell, which Cliopatria gives to Norman England from 1072) plus Gwent and Morgannwg cells as above. The Bernard page has him an invader only from 1088 ('Shortly after the settlement with the king, Bernard spearheaded an invasion of Brycheiniog'), with lands in Herefordshire in 1086/87; nothing opened dates a Norman hold on east Brycheiniog in 1072 (page silent).

correction.text: the 1072 shape (Brycheiniog proper less its eastern edge) carried to the conquest

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1085-1093: Cliopatria's row ends in 1084, but the kingdom lasted until the Norman conquest: 'invasion of Brycheiniog' in 1088 with Glasbury 'captured by autumn 1088', 'the conquest of Brycheiniog was mostly finished by Eastertide 1093', Rhys ap Tewdwr 'slain by the Frenchmen who were inhabiting Brycheiniog' in April 1093 (Rhys page), the lordship of Brecon made 'out of the ruins of the Welsh kingdom'. The page gives no area; Welsh forces retook the province briefly in 1095.

region.text: Brycheiniog, 'the southern and larger part of the historic county of Brecknockshire'

ledger.note: c. 450: Brychan founds Brycheiniog. 'Founded by Brychan Brycheiniog: c.450' (infobox) after 'Roman Britain'; the text says it was 'probably founded by Irish raiders in the late fifth century' and 'Traditionally, it was founded by and named after a legendary Hiberno-Welsh prince named Brychan'. The page names no boundary; Cliopatria's first shape begins in 540.

region.text: Brycheiniog, absorbed in the Wales of Gruffydd ap Llywelyn

ledger.note: 1056: Brycheiniog disappears into Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's Wales. Cliopatria's Gwynedd shape of 1056-1065 (23,247 km2) covers the ten Brycheiniog cells; the Gruffydd page says he ruled all Wales from 1055 to 1063 and never mentions Brycheiniog (page silent), while the Brycheiniog infobox ends the kingdom c. 1045 with the death of Gryfydd ap Elisedd.

region.text: Brycheiniog proper, one of 'the traditional kingdoms'

ledger.note: 5 August 1063: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn dies and Wales divides. 'his realm was divided again into the traditional kingdoms' (Harold's settlement gave Gwynedd and Powys to Bleddyn and Rhiwallon); Brycheiniog is not named. Cliopatria restarts the row in 1066.

region.text: two cells on the eastern and south-eastern edge: one on the Herefordshire side of the Wye, one on the Gwent border near Crickhowell

ledger.note: 1072: two border cells pass to Norman England in Cliopatria. The Bernard page has Normans in Herefordshire but dates nothing in Brycheiniog before the 1088 invasion (page silent).

region.text: Glasbury and the Wye valley: 'Glasbury was captured by autumn 1088'

ledger.note: 1088: Bernard de Neufmarché invades Brycheiniog. 'Shortly after the settlement with the king, Bernard spearheaded an invasion of Brycheiniog which was to lead eventually to its conquest'; Glasbury was captured by autumn 1088 (a charter to Gloucester's abbey).

April 1093: Rhys ap Tewdwr falls at Brecon and the conquest is 'mostly finished by Eastertide 1093'. The Rhys page gives his death as April 1093 in Brecon, 'slain by the Frenchmen who were inhabiting Brycheiniog'; the Bernard page says 1093 'or perhaps 1094' for the battle; Welsh forces briefly retook the province in 1095.

region.text: 'The lands of Brycheiniog became Bernard's Lordship of Brecknock'

ledger.note: 1093: Brycheiniog becomes the Lordship of Brecknock. 'It was conquered and pacified by the Normans between 1088 and 1095' and 'The lands of Brycheiniog became Bernard's Lordship of Brecknock'; the Bernard page: 'Out of the ruins of the Welsh kingdom he created the Anglo-Norman lordship of Brecon'.

1093: the Welsh kingdom of Brycheiniog ends. The infobox has c. 1045; the text the Norman conquest of 1088-1095. This dossier takes the death of Rhys at Brecon in April 1093 (the Bruts) as the end; Cliopatria's row stops in 1084.

wars.name: Battle of Ffinnant
wars.outcome: The Harleian Chronicle: 'Ithel ap Hywel (king of Gwent) was killed by men from Brycheiniog in the Battle of Ffinnant'; no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Norse devastation of Brycheiniog, Gwent and Gwynllwg
wars.outcome: 'in the spring of 896, Brycheiniog, Gwent and Gwynllwg were devastated by the Norsemen'; a raid, no territorial result.
wars.note: Part of the Viking army of 892-896 (Alfred the Great page, opened for the Wessex dossier).

wars.name: Æthelflæd's invasion of Brycheiniog
wars.outcome: 'in the early summer of 916, pushed her advantage by invading Brycheiniog. On 19 June, Æthelflæd stormed the royal llys (court) in Llangorse lake'; no land is said to have been annexed.
wars.note: The page gives no reason; it follows Elisse's 880s vassalage to Alfred. 918: Hywel Dda, Clydog and Idwal Foel gave allegiance to Edward the Elder (Edward page, opened for the Wessex dossier); Brycheiniog is not named.

wars.name: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's unification of Wales
wars.outcome: He 'killed his rival Gruffudd ap Rhydderch in battle and recaptured Deheubarth' in 1055, seized Gwent and Morgannwg 'around this time' and ruled all Wales to 5 August 1063; the page does not mention Brycheiniog.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Brycheiniog

zones.text: Brycheiniog: the Usk valley, Talgarth, Bronllys, Ystradyw

wars.outcome: Bernard de Neufmarché's invasion of 1088, Glasbury by autumn 1088, the battle of Brecon in April 1093 where Rhys ap Tewdwr was killed, the Lordship of Brecon; a Welsh revolt from spring 1094 retakes the province in 1095 before Glamorgan expeditions relieve the Norman garrisons.
wars.note: Bleddyn ap Maenarch is called a king 'from much later accounts' and 'there is no contemporary reference' to him (Bernard page).

certainty.note: The page describes no boundaries (reviewer eu-11-d: the words 'No boundaries are described' are not on the page; it says only that the kingdom 'later formed the southern and larger part of the historic county of Brecknockshire'); Cliopatria's ten-cell outline is the only shape, and the historic county of Brecknockshire is the page's gloss.

sources.title: Brycheiniog

sources.title: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn
sources.note: Wales united 1055-1063 under one king; Deheubarth 1055; Gwent and Morgannwg after 1055; death 5 August 1063 and division into the traditional kingdoms; silent on Brycheiniog.

sources.title: Bernard de Neufmarché
sources.note: 1088 invasion of Brycheiniog, Glasbury, the conquest mostly finished by Eastertide 1093, the Lordship of Brecon, Welsh revolt of 1094-1095.

sources.title: Rhys ap Tewdwr
sources.note: Rhys of Deheubarth 1078-1093, killed April 1093 'by the Frenchmen who were inhabiting Brycheiniog'; silent on whether he ruled Brycheiniog.

sources.title: Hywel Dda
sources.note: Hywel 'King of Brycheiniog c. 930-950' (infobox), Brycheiniog left to his sons, 918 submission to Edward; silent on any Brycheiniog king.

notes:
Page budget (5) spent on Brycheiniog, Gruffydd ap Llywelyn, Bernard de Neufmarché, Rhys ap Tewdwr and Hywel Dda. Cliopatria's five shapes are one ten-cell outline (1,962 km2) for 540-1055 and 1063-1084 with two exceptions: the 1066-1084 shapes add Gwent and Morgannwg cells (corrected away) and the 1072 shape loses two eastern cells to Norman England (kept, confidence 1). Cliopatria has no row for 1056-1065 and ends in 1084.
Dates: the infobox gives the founding c. 450 and the end 'c. 1045' (death of Gryfydd ap Elisedd), the text the Norman conquest 1088-1095; this dossier takes 450 and April 1093. The 1056-1062 gap is Cliopatria's Gwynedd shape; whether Brycheiniog was annexed or only a client of Gruffydd ap Llywelyn is not in the pages opened (his page never mentions Brycheiniog), so the 1056 loss is confidence 1.
Overlordships not in this ledger (the schema puts a vassal event in the suzerain's ledger): Alfred of Wessex ('in the 880s Elisse became a vassal of Alfred', Brycheiniog page; recorded in the Wessex dossier, confidence 1), Athelstan's tribute from Dryffin (undated, 'Athelstan era') and Tewdwr's attendance at the English court in 934, and Hywel Dda's 'King of Brycheiniog c. 930-950' with Brycheiniog 'left to Hywel's sons' (Seisyllwg/Deheubarth ledger; Cliopatria's Seisyllwg shape does not touch Brycheiniog). Æthelflæd's 916 raid is a war with no zone; Mercia's ledger can mirror it.
Gwent and Morgannwg: the 9 cells that the 1066 shape takes from them need Gwent and Morgannwg dossiers that run past 1055; the Gruffydd page says he seized both 'around this time'. Counterparts that need dossiers: lordship-of-brecon (Marcher lordship, 1093-). Deheubarth (Rhys ap Tewdwr, 1078-1093) has no Cliopatria row.
Gazetteer names needed: Talgarth, Brecon, Glasbury (places) and Brycheiniog/Brecknockshire (region; Brecknockshire lies in Powys).
